pr_title: Fix(todo-editor): resolve the configured GitHub issue repository
verdict: READY TO MERGE - 3 of 3 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: Behavioral test: calls the real config_value(config_data(), key) over the real loaded defaults and fails on CaptureError, with no stubs or mock chains.
test_the_scan_finds_the_known_lookups pins known keys so an empty or broken regex scan cannot make the parametrized check pass vacuously.
WALK_ROOTS = ('plugins/',) is declared as select_tests.py requires, and the script is loaded by absolute path with sys.modules registration like the sibling pr_review tests.

Docstring agrees with the code: config --get reads the flattened dataclass data (todo.gh_repo), make_project() with no config writes no harness.json, and the autouse fixture deactivates the config after each test.
Failure message names the prompt file, key and underlying error, so a bad prompt is located directly.

todo-editor.md:44 now asks for `todo.gh_repo`, the key `config_value` in pr_review.py:1975-1984 resolves against the dataclass from `asdict(active())` (config.py:153 `gh_repo`), so the lookup no longer exits with `unknown key`.

Every mention of the key in the agent changed together (lines 44, 192, 193), with no `todo.gh.repo` lookup left anywhere in the plugin prompts; todo_sync.py:49 and :65 correctly keep the harness.json form because they speak to the developer.
The v0.7.1 release table moves harness to 0.65.4, matching plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json at the head, and the Patch header still holds.

The release line describes the defect, its cause (flattened vs nested key) and the new guard accurately; tests/contract/test_config_get_keys.py does scan every agent and SKILL.md `config --get` key against the plugin defaults as claimed.
The fix is correct at the source: config_value walks asdict(active()), and config.py:451 flattens `todo.gh.repo` into `TodoConfig.gh_repo`, so `todo.gh_repo` is the only form that resolves.

The new contract test is behavioral and can fail: it runs the real pr_review.config_value against a config loaded from plugin defaults, and reverting todo-editor.md to `todo.gh.repo` raises CaptureError ('unknown key').

test_the_scan_finds_the_known_lookups guards against a vacuous pass. Its known set covers a first, middle and last `--get` across two multi-key calls, so a regex that stopped matching chained keys would fail it.

The test meets the repo's selection rules: it declares WALK_ROOTS for its glob walk, spells `pr_review.py` in its source, and relies on the conftest autouse deactivate so no activated config leaks between tests.
todo-editor.md now spells out that the lookup key (`todo.gh_repo`) differs from the setting a developer writes (`todo.gh.repo`), which removes the ambiguity that caused the bug.

The version bump (0.65.3 -> 0.65.4) and the release-table update agree, and the release note says accurately that the failure hit every todo-edit, add-todo and sync-gh-todo run, since the Environment lookup runs for every operation.

minor.name: Release line lacks the PR number its siblings carry
minor.summary:
docs/RELEASES/v0.7.1.md:33 opens `- Fix(todo-editor): ...` while every other entry in the Changes list leads with its PR number (`- #253 Fix(...)` at line 17, `- #255 Fix(...)` at lines 22 and 28). The GitHub release body is this file, so the todo-editor fix is the one change a reader cannot trace back to its pull request.

Also (overall): The other Changes entries in docs/RELEASES/v0.7.1.md start with the PR that landed them (`#253 Fix(...)`, `#255 Fix(...)`). The new todo-editor entry starts with a bare `Fix(todo-editor):`, so the GitHub release body built from this file will not link it to PR #257.
fix: Change line 33 to `- #257 Fix(todo-editor): the agent looks up ...`, and add `(issue #N)` after the title if an issue tracks the bug, matching lines 17 and 22.
Prefix line 33 with the PR number: `- #257 Fix(todo-editor): ...`.

minor.name: Key-form note sits in the level-2 research bullet, not at the lookup it explains
minor.summary: The new sentence `The lookup key is todo.gh_repo; the setting a developer writes in .claude/harness.json is todo.gh.repo.` sits in plugins/harness/agents/todo-editor.md:193-194, inside the add operation's Research level 2 bullet. The lookup that caused the bug is the Environment line at :44-46, which every operation (retire, split, sync, add, refresh) runs and which has no note. A later editor fixing that line to match the documented harness.json form (`todo.gh.repo`, as todo_sync.py:49 and :65 write it) would get no warning there. The contract test catches the regression, but the prose explanation belongs where the key is spelled out.
fix: Move the sentence to the end of the Environment bullet at lines 44-46 (for example, after `the third is the owner/name repository issues live in`, add `(the lookup key is todo.gh_repo; .claude/harness.json stores it as todo.gh.repo)`), and leave the level-2 bullet at lines 192-193 referring to `the todo.gh_repo line`.

minor.name: Scan skips skill reference files and commands
minor.summary:
_prompt_files collects only plugins/*/agents/*.md and plugins/*/skills/**/SKILL.md. A `pr_review.py config --get <key>` call placed in a skill's references/*.md or another prompt markdown file is never checked, so the guard the docstring promises ('every config --get an agent or skill prompt asks for') is silent for it. Today a grep of plugins/**/*.md finds the four calls only in agents and SKILL.md files, so nothing is missed yet.

Also (overall): _prompt_files() globs only `*/agents/*.md` and `*/skills/**/SKILL.md`, but harness skills ship companion prompt text that agents load as instructions: plugins/harness/skills/pr-team/canonical_prompt_template.md, pr-team/return_contract.md and pr-review/operating_rules.md. None holds a `config --get` call today, so nothing is broken. A lookup added to one of them later would go unchecked, though, and that is the same class of bug this PR fixes. The module docstring promises coverage of every 'agent or skill prompt'.
fix: Glob plugins/*/skills/**/*.md (and plugins/*/commands/*.md when present) instead of SKILL.md only; test_the_scan_finds_the_known_lookups still guards against an empty scan.
Reword the docstring to state that only agent files and SKILL.md files are scanned.
Widen line 34 to `skills = _PLUGINS.glob("*/skills/**/*.md")` so every markdown file under a skill is scanned (WALK_ROOTS already covers `plugins/`).
Or keep the narrow glob and narrow the module docstring (line 1) to 'agent files and SKILL.md files', so the scope it claims matches what it scans.
